before: In: the incident. Out: a brief / Given a transported-hazmat accident (material, container, location, time), it fuses public federal data into a structured protective action footprint, a set of sourced flags, and a draft ICS 201 Incident Briefing. / Distances trace to the PHMSA Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG). / The server runs no dispersion model; the application draws a labelled modelled cloud. / No tool result and no ICS 201 carries a modelled value.
after: In: the incident. Out: a brief / Given a hazmat accident in transport (material, container, place, time), it gathers public federal data into the area to protect, warnings that each name their source, and a draft Incident Command System briefing form (ICS 201). / Every distance comes from the federal Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG). / The server runs no dispersion model; the application draws a labelled modelled cloud. / No tool result and no ICS 201 carries a modelled value.

before: The modelled cloud by health-effect level, on a clock / it draws one modelled cloud by health-effect level (AEGL-3, AEGL-2 and AEGL-1) from the one engine a held criterion names for the release / held as a frame every 15 minutes of cloud time on a coarse mesh whose level outlines are drawn from it, each frame shown as it is computed, with one Play control off by default / The ERG footprint is the protective action distance.
after: The modelled gas cloud, by level of health effect, over time / The application draws one modelled cloud for each level of health effect (Acute Exposure Guideline Levels AEGL-3, AEGL-2 and AEGL-1), from the one model a published test chooses for the release. / The cloud is drawn for every 15 minutes of its time, each step shown as soon as it is computed, with a Play control. / The protective action distance is the guidebook's.

before: One engine per release, and a receipt on every number / the critical Richardson number of NOAA's NOS OR&R 43 classes the release dense, passive or not classed / A dense release is drawn by SCICHEM, run in a separate models image on the forecast wind hour by hour / A release the criterion cannot class draws neither and says why / A receipt is a tool output path with its value, or a document and page. / csx night, first frame of the cloud; page before and after: 14.2 s; 6.62 MB, then 3.39 MB
after: One model per release, and a source on every number / A published test (the critical Richardson number) classes the release as a dense gas, a gas that drifts with the air, or not classed. / A dense gas is modelled by SCICHEM, a dispersion model from the Electric Power Research Institute, on the forecast wind, hour by hour. / A release the test cannot class is not modelled, and the brief says why. / Every number carries its source: the tool output it came from, with its value, or a document and page. / Point of Rocks night scenario, first picture of the cloud; the page's size before and after a fix: 14.2 seconds; 6.62 megabytes, then 3.39 megabytes

before: How it is tested, at four levels and a gate / Every collected test runs in exactly one of the two steps, and both must pass. / Level | What it tests / Part A: exhaustive invariant checks | Every output the tools can produce obeys the invariants. / Part B: scenario regression | That no change moves any tool output on any frozen scenario unnoticed. / Part C: live drift | Whether the federal sources the server reads at runtime still answer as they did when the fixtures were recorded. / Part D: the agent evaluation | Is every number and name in its reply grounded in a tool output?
after: How it is tested: four levels, two steps / Every collected test runs in exactly one of the two steps, and both must pass. / Level | What it tests / Part A: fixed rules on every output | Every output the tools can produce obeys the server's fixed rules. / Part B: saved scenarios rerun | No change moves any tool output on any saved scenario unnoticed. / Part C: live sources | Whether the federal sources the server reads still answer as they did when the test scenarios were recorded. / Part D: the language model's replies | Is every number and name in its reply backed by a tool output?
